card.one_sentence_claim: SBT reproduces the structural skeleton "a classical symmetry can fail to survive quantization" as a layer-agnostic, Lean-certified descent-obstruction normal form (F40): a would-be symmetry gate is anomalous iff it fails at least one of {SymmetryDescends, DomainDescends, GroupLawPreserved, ReadoutPreserved} on the formed-layer quotient — supplying the descent test, not the QFT anomaly content (triangle diagram, index theorem, cancellation condition).
card.target_known_fact: In QFT a classical symmetry can fail to survive quantization (an anomaly), and gauge anomalies must cancel for consistency. The structural feature being targeted is specifically "a classical symmetry fails to descend to the quantized/formed layer," together with the descent-equation/Wess-Zumino-consistency posture that anomalies are obstructions to a symmetry passing to a quotient. The quantitative content (anomaly coefficient from the triangle diagram, Atiyah-Singer index theorem, the SM/string cancellation conditions fixing matter content) is NOT targeted.

card.baseline_comparison: SBT does strictly LESS than the standard account, and only RECOVERS (reorganizes) a structural posture rather than deriving any anomaly result. The standard QFT account both (a) explains why a symmetry fails to survive quantization via a concrete mechanism (non-invariant path-integral measure / triangle diagram / index theorem) AND (b) computes the anomaly coefficient and derives the cancellation conditions that fix matter content (SM hypercharges, Green-Schwarz). SBT's F40 reproduces ONLY the qualitative skeleton '(a) is a failure of a symmetry gate to descend through a quotient,' with the mechanism and ALL quantitative content (b) imported by declaration/citation. F40's genuine value-add over an ad hoc statement is that it is a single Lean-certified normal form unifying this descent failure across non-physics domains (IEEE-754, gimbal lock, lattice, arbitrage, Galilean vs relativistic addition). The descent/cohomological reading of anomalies (anomaly = obstruction to passing a symmetry to a quotient) is, however, ALREADY standard in the math-physics literature (descent equations, equivariant cohomology, BRST), so even the organizing lens is not novel to SBT. Net: recovers the structural feature, reorganizes it as one instance of the F2/F40 descent family; does not do better than, and does materially less than, the standard account on the physics.
card.why_scientists_care: Anomalies sit at the heart of QFT consistency (gauge-anomaly cancellation fixes the SM matter content and underlies anomaly-inflow / 't Hooft matching). A claim that this is an instance of a generic, machine-checked 'descent obstruction' is conceptually appealing because it would unify it with coarse-graining failures elsewhere in physics and computation. The honest scientific interest is narrow but real: F40 cleanly SEPARATES the universal structural skeleton (a symmetry failing to pass to a quotient) from the domain-specific anomaly content, making explicit exactly which pieces (Jacobian, index theorem, cocycle, cancellation) are irreducibly QFT. It is a clarifying organizational lens, not a new physics result.

No new Lean code is required.
card.execution_cost: Low. F40 and F2 are already proved and Lean-certified (faithful = no narrowing debt); the minimum viable result is a worked exposition + a structural correspondence table, requiring no new theorems, no numerics, and no Lean development. Only literature cross-checking (Bertlmann; SM/string anomaly cancellation) and careful scope-writing are needed. The stronger (bridge) result is High-to-prohibitive cost and blocked by the disclaimed missing continuum/path-integral interface.
card.honest_status_note: Grounded and faithful at the skeleton level; over-claimable at the physics level. F40 (Symmetry.Anomaly.anomaly_symmetry_obstruction) and its engine F2 (Transport.DescentRepair.descent_repair_normal_form) are genuinely Lean-certified with 'faithful' semantic alignment (no narrowing debt) — they are elementary, finite, true-by-quotient-universal-property statements (verified: F40 proof, lines 3345-3376, is the standard 'constant on fibers' argument; F2 proof, line 2337, explicitly cites 'the quotient universal property'). 'faithful' is a Lean-semantic grade (base wording, no narrowing debt; lines 9810-9811), NOT a claim of fidelity to QFT anomalies. The paper itself states F40 'does not classify anomalies into carrier-specific forms' (line 3380) and routes all QFT content to Bertlmann 2000 (line 3385). This card claims ONLY recovery of the structural feature 'a classical symmetry can fail to descend,' with the quantization quotient and symmetry gate supplied by declaration. The card crosses NO SBT disclaimer provided two boundaries are honored: (1) it does not claim to derive the anomaly (mechanism, coefficient, index theorem) and (2) it does not claim to explain anomaly CANCELLATION — which F40 structurally cannot express. Derivability class C (structural reorganization / forced-target), not a derivation. The only honest novelty is organizational unification of descent failure across domains, and even that organizing lens (anomaly = descent obstruction) pre-exists in the math-physics literature.

adhoc_test_answers.question: 1. Was the target fact known before the theory component was built?
adhoc_test_answers.answer: Yes. QFT anomalies, Wess-Zumino consistency, and anomaly cancellation are decades-old textbook facts (Bertlmann 2000 cited inside F40). The target is forced (argument_family = forced-target). F40 is a general quotient-descent statement written with the anomaly target in view.

adhoc_test_answers.question: 2. Does the theory derive the fact, or only accommodate / re-describe it?
adhoc_test_answers.answer: Only re-describes (derivability_class C, structural reorganization). F40 is the quotient universal property (a map descends iff constant on fibers / obstruction set empty) reskinned as 'anomaly' (verified: lines 3345-3376). It derives NO anomaly content: not the triangle-diagram coefficient, not the index theorem, not the WZ cocycle, and structurally cannot express cancellation. The card concedes all of this.

adhoc_test_answers.question: 3. How many free/adjustable parameters feed the match, and are any fixed only post hoc?
adhoc_test_answers.answer: At least 7 explicit declared objects (gate alpha, group G, domain D, readout r, value action rho, quotient q, candidate bar-alpha) plus the lens/basis implicit choice. ALL are fixed post hoc by declaration; none is derived or pinned before comparison. The QFT mapping is purely declarative.

adhoc_test_answers.question: 4. Are the parameters physically motivated or curve-fitting knobs?
adhoc_test_answers.answer: They are structural slots, not curve-fit numerics (data_points_matched = 0). But for the QFT claim they are unconstrained declaration knobs: SBT supplies no principle selecting the quantization quotient or pointer basis (explicitly disclaimed), so the 'physical motivation' is imported from QFT, not provided by SBT.

adhoc_test_answers.question: 5. Does the same mechanism explain multiple independent facts, or is it one-off?
adhoc_test_answers.answer: The mechanism (quotient-descent / split-pair obstruction) is heavily reused: F2 descent-repair, F10 quotientality, F18 lawhood descent, F27 conservation-as-orbit-descent, F15a selection obstruction, plus the five non-QFT instantiations. So the engine is general (a plus for non-adhocness of the ENGINE), but its application to the QFT anomaly is one declared instance with zero derived content. The descent-obstruction reading of anomalies pre-exists in the literature, so even the lens is not novel.

adhoc_test_answers.question: 6. Would the opposite observation have been equally explainable?
adhoc_test_answers.answer: Yes, trivially. By choosing q, r, or D differently, the same machinery declares a symmetry anomalous (nonempty obstruction) OR non-anomalous (empty obstruction). F2 explicitly provides 'repairs' (source refinement / target coarsening, lines 2313-2317) that flip the verdict. F40 is a definitional iff with no predictive constraint.

adhoc_test_answers.question: 7. Is the match quantitative and risky, or qualitative and safe?
adhoc_test_answers.answer: Qualitative and safe. No quantitative content whatsoever (data_points_matched = 0). It is a structural concordance table, so there is no risky numerical prediction that could have failed.

adhoc_test_answers.question: 8. Does the match cross any SBT disclaimer (continuum, Born rule, pointer basis, etc.)?
adhoc_test_answers.answer: Not at the skeleton level, IF two boundaries are honored: (i) no claim to derive anomaly mechanism/coefficient/index theorem, (ii) no claim to explain cancellation. The stronger 'bridge' (Fujikawa Jacobian as ReadoutPreserved failure) WOULD cross the disclaimed no-continuum / no-path-integral interface (ledger missing_interfaces #4) and the pointer-basis disclaimer. The card correctly marks the bridge as out of scope, so the minimum-viable claim stays just inside the disclaimers but only because it asserts almost nothing physical.

opposite_world_test.explanation: In an opposite world where a classical symmetry DID survive quantization (no anomaly), F40 explains it equally well: the obstruction sets O_alpha, O_D are empty, GroupLawPreserved and ReadoutPreserved hold, so SymmetryDescends is true. F40 is a biconditional definition (anomaly iff at least one of four descent conditions fails), not a prediction, so BOTH the anomalous and non-anomalous worlds are 'retrodicted' with no change to the machinery. Worse, for any FIXED physical case the verdict is tunable: the quotient q and readout r are declared externally with no canonical-lens principle (disclaimed), and F2 explicitly supplies source-refinement / target-coarsening 'repairs' (thm:F2, line 2313) that turn a nonempty obstruction empty. So SBT could be made to declare a real anomaly absent, or a non-anomalous symmetry anomalous, purely by re-choosing q or r. The framework has zero risk: it cannot predict the sign/presence of an anomaly, the anomaly coefficient, or which matter content cancels (no additive structure). It only records, after the physics is supplied by declaration, which descent box was ticked.

audit.audit_verdict: HIGH FLEXIBILITY / LOW RISK, HONEST AT SKELETON LEVEL. R031 is a forced-target, derivability-class-C structural reorganization with 0 data points matched and ~7 freely-declared structural parameters plus an undetermined lens/quotient choice. F40 (Symmetry.Anomaly.anomaly_symmetry_obstruction) is genuinely Lean-certified 'faithful' (table line 10077; all 46 direct rows faithful, lines 9822-9823), but it is an elementary quotient-universal-property biconditional: a map/action/predicate descends through q iff its obstruction set is empty (thm:F40, lines 3310-3342; proof is the standard 'constant on fibers' argument, lines 3345-3376). The mechanism is the same orbit/quotient-descent engine reused across F2, F10, F18, F27, F15a -- a real organizational unification, so the ENGINE is not ad hoc. But the APPLICATION to QFT anomalies derives nothing: the triangle diagram, index theorem, Wess-Zumino cocycle, descent equations, and (critically) anomaly cancellation are all imported by the Bertlmann 2000 citation (line 3385), and F40 explicitly 'does not classify anomalies into carrier-specific forms' (line 3380) and has no additive structure to express cancellation. The opposite-world test FAILS: F40 'retrodicts' both anomalous and non-anomalous worlds, and the verdict on any fixed case is tunable via the externally declared quotient q / readout r and the F2 'repair' operations. imports_known_physics = true; target_used_to_design_theory = true. The minimum-viable claim crosses NO disclaimer ONLY because it asserts essentially no physics; the 'stronger' Fujikawa-bridge claim WOULD cross the disclaimed no-continuum / no-path-integral interface (missing_interfaces #4) and is correctly shelved.
